claims.claim: Source claims eight paid apps have been 'cloned' for free by AI.
Epic Vibe-coded launcher reportedly starts 46% faster than Steam 'in its own test'.
Fortnite can be launched inside Steam by adding it as a shortcut to the library.
'Cloud motion' is a free and open tool to make motion videos from a prompt with a coding agent.
A free Superhuman-like client offers fast Gmail/Outlook access with AI sorting and drafted replies.
A from-scratch Figma rebuild supports auto-layout, components, prototypes, offline use, and no account.
A free open Office clone opens Word/Excel/PowerPoint files.
An open-source Intercom alternative support desk includes AI agents.
A newsletter tool is claimed 67% cheaper ($39 vs $119/month at 10,000 readers).

recommendations.application: Treat the 'Superhuman free' and prompt-to-motion claims as inspiration only; Personafy already has local vision writing, adapters, and generation/review/publishing gates. No new file creation or modification is warranted. If pursued at all, this would be a external evaluation of an email/LLM drafting UX pattern as a reading exercise, not an implementation.

No credible, specific use. General 'AI tool' hype does not map to paper-trading research, evidence capture, or governance. At most, the newsletter/client tooling mentions are unrelated to trading research.

If anything, use this only as a lead-generation prompt: verify each claimed tool by name/license/repo before any evaluation. The Office-compatibility and prompt-to-motion categories are the most testable against existing needs; the launcher/Fortnite claims are consumer-facing and irrelevant here.
